precepts.text: A Psalm of David when he fled from Absalom his son; the Lord is a shield for him, sustaining him in sleep though ten thousands set themselves against him.
precepts.point: The two came up out of the well and told David to arise and pass quickly over the water. David and all the people passed over Jordan by the morning light, and there lacked not one of them that was not gone over.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

precepts.why:
This is a Psalm of David when he fled from Absalom his son: “Lord, how are they increased that trouble me! many are they that rise up against me. Many there be which say of my soul, There is no help for him in God.” But “thou, O Lord, art a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head.”

That is this night. Hushai sent word by Zadok and Abiathar: “Lodge not this night in the plains of the wilderness, but speedily pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that are with him.” Jonathan and Ahimaaz waited by En-rogel and a wench carried the word to them. A lad saw them and told Absalom, so they hid in a well in a man’s house in Bahurim, and a woman spread a covering over the well’s mouth and ground corn upon it to camouflage it. She told Absalom’s servants, “They be gone over the brook of water”, and the pursuers returned to Jerusalem.

The Most High put his spirit on certain people to orchestrate his plan. Often when a man tries to do evil to another, it falls back on him, for he that diggeth a pit shall fall therein.

“I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the Lord sustained me. I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people, that have set themselves against me round about.” David arose and all the people with him passed over Jordan, and “by the morning light there lacked not one of them that was not gone over Jordan.” “Salvation belongeth unto the Lord: thy blessing is upon thy people.”

note.label: Psalm 3: But Thou O Lord Art a Shield for Me

precepts.why:
“Lord, how are they increased that trouble me! many are they that rise up against me.” This is a psalm of David when he fled from Absalom his son, and Christ said this is how it goes: “Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.”

Christ came not to send peace but a sword, and a man's foes shall be they of his own household. That is exactly what David is facing in Psalm 3: his own son was out to get him, and the men who once served the king were being turned against him.

Put yourself in that position, because it may one day be your trial too. Things written the fourth time were written for our learning, that through the patience and comfort of the scriptures we might have hope.

precepts.text: Absalom rose up early and stood beside the way of the gate, and when any man came to the king for judgment Absalom flattered him and kissed him, so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
precepts.point: Lord, how are they increased that trouble me, many are they that rise up against me. Put yourself in that position: David's own son was out to get him, and the men who once served the king were being turned against him.

note.label: Psalm 3: But Thou O Lord Art a Shield for Me

precepts.why:
To know how they increased that trouble David, go back to the history: “Absalom prepared him chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him. And Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate: and it was so, that when any man that had a controversy came to the king for judgment, then Absalom called unto him”.

He asked each man, “Of what city art thou?” and told him, “See, thy matters are good and right; but there is no man deputed of the king to hear thee.” Then he said, “Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man which hath any suit or cause might come unto me, and I would do him justice!” And “when any man came nigh to him to do him obeisance, he put forth his hand, and took him, and kissed him.”

Absalom flattered every man who came to the king for judgment and kissed him, “so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.” That is how the men who once served the king were turned against David, and why he says many are they that rise up against me.

precepts.text: Absalom was making a power play, conspiring to overthrow his father, and the conspiracy was strong for the people increased continually with Absalom, so David told his servants to arise and flee lest Absalom overtake them.
precepts.point: Lord, how are they increased that trouble me, many are they that rise up against me. Put yourself in that position: David's own son was out to get him, and the men who once served the king were being turned against him.

note.label: Psalm 3: But Thou O Lord Art a Shield for Me

precepts.why:
Absalom was making a power play, conspiring to overthrow his father: “And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counsellor, from his city, even from Giloh, while he offered sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong; for the people increased continually with Absalom.”

The people increased continually with Absalom; that is “how are they increased that trouble me!” “And there came a messenger to David, saying, The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom. And David said unto all his servants that were with him at Jerusalem, Arise, and let us flee; for we shall not else escape from Absalom: make speed to depart, lest he overtake us suddenly, and bring evil upon us, and smite the city with the edge of the sword.”

David told his servants to arise and flee lest Absalom overtake them. Read the psalm remembering this heading: David fleeing from his own son. If you do not know that history, go back to Second Samuel and read it, and put yourself in the scriptures to better your understanding.

precepts.text: Behold, the eye of the Lord is upon them that fear Him, upon them that hope in His mercy; our soul waiteth for the Lord, for He is our help and our shield. The Most High is the help and shield David is leaning on.
precepts.point: But thou O Lord art a shield for me, my glory, and the lifter up of mine head. Think about it: your grown son gets big and bad and comes against you, yet David still trusted in the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 3: But Thou O Lord Art a Shield for Me

precepts.why:
“Many there be which say of my soul, There is no help for him in God.” David did not agree; he was a man after the Most High's own heart and trusted in Him: “Behold, the eye of the Lord is upon them that fear him, upon them that hope in his mercy; To deliver their soul from death, and to keep them alive in famine.”

“Our soul waiteth for the Lord: he is our help and our shield. For our heart shall rejoice in him, because we have trusted in his holy name. Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, according as we hope in thee.” The Most High is the help and shield David is leaning on when he says, “But thou, O Lord, art a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head.”

Think about it: your grown son gets big and bad and comes against you, and the men turn away, yet David still trusted in the Most High, whose eye is upon them that fear him and hope in his mercy.

precepts.text: Salvation belongeth unto the Most High; affirmed as a precept for Psalms 27:1 on the Most High being salvation.
precepts.point: Prayer is largely invalid if there is no action behind it. If you ask for a home but take no steps toward the finances, why would you receive it. Faith without works is dead.

note.label: Psalm 30: Joy Cometh in the Morning

precepts.why:
“Salvation belongeth unto the Lord: thy blessing is upon thy people.” When David cries “Lord, be thou my helper”, he knows where the help comes from. The Most High is salvation, the same understanding given for Psalms 27:1, and his blessing is upon his people.

He turned David's “mourning into dancing”, put off his sackcloth and “girded me with gladness”, “To the end that my glory may sing praise to thee, and not be silent.” That is the kingdom, where we will sing thanks to the Most High for ever.

But salvation belonging to the Lord does not make us idle. As Israelites we seek a country, the kingdom and this world back, and we must make that request known plainly. And prayer is largely invalid if there is no action behind it: if you ask for a home but take no steps toward the finances, why would you receive it? Faith without works is dead.
